title: Testicular germ cell tumor
subtitle: Most common solid malignancy in males 15–35 · >90% cure, >95% 5-yr survival — chemotherapy is curative even in advanced disease · lung is the commonest met site (62%); liver (16%) and brain (7%) are negative prognostic factors
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Testicular Cancer (Moore K, Glover M, Shah S) · NCCN v1.2025 · trial data verified against the primary publications

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Suspicious mass: H&P, AFP, bHCG, LDH, chemistry, testicular ultrasound
Repeat all markers after orchiectomy — TNM staging uses post-orchiectomy values
Pure seminoma (seminoma histology + normal AFP; bHCG may be elevated): abdominal/pelvic CT + chest X-ray; chest CT only if abdominal CT positive or CXR abnormal
Non-seminoma (incl. mixed, and seminoma histology with elevated AFP): chest/abdominal/pelvic CT up front
Both: brain MRI if clinically indicated · sperm banking
Nodal spread is predictable — right-sided to inter-aortocaval, left-sided to para-aortic

blocks.heading: Histology → marker pattern
rows: AFP and/or hCG; commonest mixed component
blocks.footnote: Seminoma hCG comes from syncytiotrophoblasts and is compatible with pure seminoma — only AFP reclassifies. Very high hCG in choriocarcinoma can cause hyperthyroidism (TSH receptor cross-reactivity) and gynecomastia. LDH is non-specific and tracks tumor bulk. Teratoma is marker-negative and chemoresistant — the reason post-chemotherapy masses must be resected.

blocks.heading: Serum tumor markers (S)
blocks.footnote: hCG mIU/mL, AFP ng/mL. pT1a/pT1b (<3 vs ≥3 cm) applies to pure seminoma only. cN1 ≤2 cm · cN2 >2–5 cm · cN3 >5 cm. M1a nodal/pulmonary · M1b non-pulmonary visceral.

blocks.heading: IGCCCG risk — the asymmetry
rows: Good: testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP<1,000 + hCG<5,000 + LDH<1.5×. Intermediate: markers in the middle band. Poor: mediastinal primary, non-pulmonary visceral mets, or AFP>10,000 / hCG>50,000 / LDH>10×
Good: any primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, normal AFP. Intermediate: non-pulmonary visceral mets. There is no poor-risk category — only AFP matters, not hCG or LDH

boxes: alt: carboplatin ×1–2 or RT (risk factor >4 cm)
seminoma: RT or RPLND if IIA / non-bulky IIB
seminoma IIC treated as BEP ×3 / EP ×4
seminoma >3 cm: PET — avid resect, non-avid observe
relapse: resect, else TIP/VeIP ×4 or HDCT

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: The AFP rule overrides histology. Pure seminoma requires seminoma histology and a normal AFP; seminoma histology with an elevated AFP is worked up and treated as a non-seminoma. Elevated bHCG is compatible with pure seminoma

Dose holds and reductions are discouraged in the curative (1st and 2nd line) setting — delay only for severe active infection or illness. The one stated exception: hold or reduce cisplatin for creatinine >1.5 (EP)
Residual mass rules differ by histology — PET works for seminoma but not non-seminoma, because teratoma is not FDG-avid yet is chemoresistant and must be resected
Non-pulmonary visceral metastases define intermediate-risk seminoma and poor-risk non-seminoma
RT or RPLND remains an option only for stage IIA and non-bulky IIB seminoma (nodes <3 cm)
Sperm banking before treatment; restage markers after orchiectomy

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: cisplatin 20/day d1–5 · etoposide 100/day d1–5 · bleomycin 30 units d1, 8, 15 · filgrastim d6–12
etoposide 100/day d1–5 · cisplatin 20/day d1–5 · pegfilgrastim d5→6
etoposide 75 · ifosfamide 1200 · cisplatin 20, all d1–5 · mesna · pegfilgrastim d6
paclitaxel 250 d1 · ifosfamide 1500 d2–5 · cisplatin 25 d2–5 · mesna
vinblastine 0.11 mg/kg d1–2 · ifosfamide 1200 d1–5 · cisplatin 20 d1–5 · mesna
carboplatin 700 + etoposide 750 — days −5, −4, −3 before stem-cell infusion, ×2 cycles
gemcitabine + paclitaxel ± oxaliplatin · oxaliplatin + irinotecan · oral etoposide 50–100 mg d1–21
200 mg q3wk (or 400 mg q6wk) — MSI-H, dMMR, or TMB >10
blocks.footnote: All doses mg/m² unless stated. Growth factor support is built into every first- and second-line regimen; mesna with every ifosfamide-containing regimen.

blocks.heading: Landmark trials
rows: 2021 (n=9,728): 5-yr OS good 96% / int 89% / poor 67% (was 91/79/48); adds LDH >2.5× ULN
3 vs 4 BEP, favorable risk — NED 98% vs 97%. n=184
3 vs 4 BEP and 5- vs 3-day — 2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%, equivalent
Single-arm n=289, good risk — CR 98%. Bleomycin-free option
Stage I seminoma: carboplatin AUC7 ×1 non-inferior to RT (5-yr RFS 94.7% vs 96.0%)
Seminoma RT 20 Gy = 30 Gy, less lethargy
CS I non-sem 1×BEP: 5-yr relapse 3.2% LVI+ / 1.6% LVI− vs 41.7% / 13.2% surveillance
Ongoing phase 3, TIP vs TI-CE at first salvage, primary OS
blocks.footnote: Phase 3 only for the BEP-cycle and seminoma-RT questions. SWENOTECA is population-based; Kondagunta TIP (ph 2), 4×EP and TI-CE (ph 1/2) are single-arm.

blocks.html: Biomarkers: testicular cancer is marker-driven, not biomarker-driven — AFP, bHCG and LDH determine stage, risk group and response. The only biomarker-selected therapy in the chapter is pembrolizumab for MSI-H, dMMR, or TMB >10.
